summary: An exceptionally complete and honest Phase 3 artifact. The full Nord Stage 4 73 surface is faithfully retained (73 keys E1-E7, six sections at documented fractions, continuous red chassis, HAMMER ACTION label) with two live-truthful OLEDs (program position/name, BPM/transpose/scene; synth waveform/filter/LFO/arp). Programs (32 slots + 8 Live, page/program/dial/list navigation, Store/Store As, truthful dirty state), splits at the 11 documented positions with Off/±6/±12 crossfade gain math, two scenes, Wheel+Control-Pedal morphs, master clock, transpose, and Panic are all present in a single serializable ProgramState. Organ (distinct B3/Vox/Farf/Pipe additive engines with drawbars+LEDs, percussion, key click, vibrato/chorus) and Synth (three layers, 14 waveforms across Pure/Sync/Multi/Super/FM-H with category-correct Osc Ctrl, LP12/LP24/HP/BP filters, three envelopes, clock-synced LFO, poly/mono/legato+glide+unison, deterministic arp/gate) are genuinely different DSP, not renamed oscillators, proven by 232 real-signal tests (correlation, spectral spread, high-band ratio) across 25 files. One AudioContext feeds six buses -> ordered effects -> master gain + limiter -> one destination. Grand/Upright/Electric ship as 108 bundled WAV takes (18 roots x 2 velocity x 3 types), truthfully declared as locally-rendered CC0 sample sets; 11 generated sources honestly declared. The live app boots with zero console errors and every control writes real canonical state (verified: program load 2.3, organ B3->Vox, synth Saw->Square, filter cutoff 127->125), with the 7 spec-excluded controls surfaced in the status bar and synth OLED. The one real gap: the shipped browser audio path drops the Rotary effect (withoutLiveUnits disables rotary and no live rotary node exists; createRotary runs only in the deterministic render used by tests), so rotary is proven in-engine but silent in the browser, and per-voice buffer pre-rendering means manual knob turns do not re-modulate already-held notes. These bound audioIntegration to strong-but-not-flawless; everything else is exemplary.

evidence: src/audio/render.ts renderGraph: piano A/B + organ (shared 'organ' chain) + synth A/B/C each run one ordered chain (Mod1->Mod2->Delay->Amp/EQ/Filter->Comp->Reverb), then rotary tap post-reverb, layer level, one master gain + tanh limiter — a single mix path; effects-graph.test.ts proves master-zero silences everything and all engines share one stereo graph.

src/audio/web-audio-backend.ts constructs ONE AudioContext with six layer-gain buses -> master gain -> DynamicsCompressor limiter -> destination, plus a live convolver reverb send/return; no separate context.

GAP: the browser path drops Rotary. withoutLiveUnits() sets clone.rotary.on=false before per-voice rendering, and the backend creates no live rotary node (grep: createRotary is used only in render.ts, i.e. the deterministic/test path). The code comment 'reverb + rotary stay live nodes' is inaccurate — only reverb is live. Rotary/To-Rotary is therefore inaudible in the shipped instrument though correct in-engine. criteria.label: Musical quality, latency, and load
evidence: Strengths: tanh master limiter bounds peaks; per-layer 16-voice polyphony with deterministic stealing; arp step timing lands in expected windows (synth.test.ts); cleanup returns voice/node/timer counts to baseline (backend.persistentNodeCount + teardown, asserted in effects-graph/organ tests); bufferCache bounded (clears >96). Live app played layered engines with zero console errors.

Limitation: WebAudioBackend pre-renders each voice into an 8 s buffer through the shared graph, so LFO/vibrato/arp animate over a note's life but MANUAL knob turns (filter cutoff, mod/delay/amp) do not re-modulate an already-held note — only subsequent notes reflect the change. Combined with the browser rotary omission above, live real-time expressive automation on sustained notes is limited, so sound quality/latency/load is strong but not flawless.

issues.title: Startup freeze from O(n·k) reverb impulse render (manually fixed post-seal)
issues.detail: The sealed artifact froze the browser main thread for ~13-16s on every load, and again on any reverb type/bright change. web-audio-backend.ts buildImpulse() rendered the convolution IR by running a unit impulse through createReverb().process(), whose direct-form convolution is O(n·k): at 48kHz that is ~172,800 samples against a ~144,000-sample IR, ~2.5e10 multiply-adds. Measured: 4 rendered frames in 16s (a 16,068ms gap with no frames) and 10/10 fresh loads failed to produce a paint within 6s; CPU profile showed 98.9% of samples in the reverb process() function. Phase 1 was unaffected (no reverb). This was fixed manually after sealing so the artifact could be published and played in the gallery: buildImpulse now assembles the buffer directly from the reverb's cached impulse response in O(n), since convolving a unit impulse with h yields h. The fix is output-identical (verified to <1e-7 across all reverb types x bright/dark) and the artifact's own suites still pass (stage2 138/138, stage3 232/232). Post-fix: 480 frames/4s, no gaps, 10/10 loads paint in 33-45ms. A 25-point deduction is applied to this phase because the delivered artifact was unusable as shipped and required manual repair.

issues.summary: Rotary effect is inaudible in the shipped browser instrument. src/audio/web-audio-backend.ts withoutLiveUnits() sets clone.rotary.on=false before per-voice rendering and the backend creates no live rotary node; createRotary() is used only in the deterministic src/audio/render.ts (the path the tests exercise). The comment 'reverb + rotary stay live nodes' is inaccurate. Rotary DSP, acceleration, stop, and To-Rotary/ORGAN routing are correct and tested in-engine but produce no audible output in the browser. Controls still write canonical state, so it is not fabricated success, but a claimed audible effect is not connected to the live signal graph.

Per-voice buffer pre-rendering (8 s) means manual knob turns (filter cutoff, mod/delay/amp/comp) do not re-modulate an already-held note in the browser; only subsequent notes reflect the change. LFO/vibrato/arp are baked into the buffer so they still animate. A reasonable engineering tradeoff, honestly non-faking, but it limits live expressive real-time automation on sustained notes.

Grand/Upright/Electric ship as 108 bundled WAV takes (verified on disk under public/samples/) but are locally rendered from the project's own physical models via scripts/render-samples.mjs rather than acoustic recordings. IMPLEMENTATION_DETAILS.json declares this truthfully (kind: recorded-sample-set, source describes local rendering, CC0) and they are offline-capable and audibly distinct, so this satisfies the honesty contract; noted only for transparency.

postSealAdjustment.reason: Startup freeze (O(n·k) reverb IR render) required a manual post-seal code fix to make the artifact viewable.
